headline: Scam ads and deepfakes impersonating Nigerian public figures stay on Facebook for months.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: full investigation read; not stale.
importance_line: What changed: Premium Times found deepfake scam ads still running months after fact-checkers flagged them, which affects people who lose money and public figures whose faces are used; the doubt is that the report covers a set of cases and does not measure how many scam ads Meta carries.
summary: Premium Times reports that deepfake videos of Nigerian figures, including Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, who represents Kogi Central in Nigeria's National Assembly, and Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, were promoted as paid Facebook ads for fake investment schemes and stayed up for months. It matters because Meta confirmed the ads broke its rules and removed them only after the newspaper asked, and Meta says it removed over 159 million scam ads on Facebook last year.
notes: Full article read. Meta statements are Meta's own. Reuters figure is a secondhand citation inside the article.
